title: Accessible tabs with keyboard support
when: The user wants content split into tabs that switch panels in place, such as specs, reviews and shipping.
prompt:
Goal: Tabs that follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, with arrow key navigation and one visible panel at a time.
Steps:
1. <div role="tablist" aria-label="..."> with <button type="button" role="tab" id="tab-x" aria-selected aria-controls="panel-x">; panels are <div role="tabpanel" id="panel-x" aria-labelledby="tab-x" tabindex="0">.
2. Roving tabindex: the selected tab has tabindex="0", the others "-1"; inactive panels carry hidden.
3. ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move with wrap, Home and End jump to the ends; select on focus when panels are instant.
4. Show the selected tab with a 3 px underline and bolder text, not color alone.
5. On narrow screens the tablist scrolls sideways (overflow-x: auto) and the active tab is scrolled into view.
Quality bar:
- Exactly one tab has aria-selected="true".
- Tab goes from the active tab straight into its panel.
- Without JS every panel shows in sequence.
Pitfalls:
- Links styled as tabs that reload the page.
- Every tab left in the Tab order.
- Panels hidden with opacity that still take focus.
Verify:
- [ ] Roles and aria-controls ids match.
- [ ] Arrows, Home and End move between tabs.
- [ ] Inactive panels have hidden.
- [ ] Ids are unique.
Output: Tabs markup in the page, tabs.css and tabs.js wiring every [role=tablist].

examples.input: abas de descricao, medidas e avaliacoes no produto
examples.output: tablist with three tabs, roving tabindex, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, panels with aria-labelledby
